title: Binary Tree from Level Order
hints: Enum values are immutable, so build children before parents.
First use a level-order queue to record each node's left/right positions; then build recursively from index 0.
`case .node(.empty, let v, .empty): v` matches leaves when summing.
jsBridge: Trees as `indirect enum Tree { case empty; case node(Tree, Int, Tree) }` make the null child a real case, like a TS union `Tree = null | {l, v, r}`, but with exhaustive pattern matching on every traversal.

compass.q: TS `type Tree = null | {left: Tree, val: number, right: Tree}` vs Swift's indirect enum: what does pattern matching give you?
Enum trees (immutable, value) vs class nodes (mutable, shared): which is easier for building from level order?
Deep, skewed trees make recursive traversal overflow the stack. How deep before it crashes?
Where do trees appear in app work: comment threads, file browsers, `OutlineGroup` in SwiftUI?
